jobs.title: Associate Director, Pension Planning and Performance Reporting (15-Month Contract)
jobs.description:
Our Company Background & Culture

UPP is the first pension plan of its kind in Ontario’s university sector, proudly serving over 46,000 members across six universities and nineteen sector organizations. Our purpose is to bring greater retirement peace of mind to the university sector by investing with integrity and serving members with care. As a sector-wide plan designed for growth, our doors are open to all Ontario universities.

We’re a team of progressive thinkers and agile doers operating within a fast-paced culture of collaboration and respect. We believe in bringing smart and capable people together to create, solve, and grow with a clear shared vision and values of integrity, inclusivity, ingenuity, and impact.

We’ve Built And Nurtured a Culture That Is Intentionally Welcoming And Purposefully Rooted In Equity, Diversity, Inclusion, And Reconciliation (EDI&R). We Believe Diverse Teams, Perspectives, And Lived Experiences Contribute To Better Decisions And a Better Workplace. As UPP Celebrates Its Fifth Anniversary, We’re Proud To Be Recognized For Our Efforts

2026 Greater Toronto’s Top 100 Employers
2026 Canadian HR Award for Excellence in Diversity, Equity, Inclusion & Belonging

Join us in building a bright future for our members, our organization, and each other.

THE ROLE

The Associate Director, Pension Planning & Performance Reporting (15-Month Contract) is accountable for leading the development and delivery of Pension Services reporting and analytics, ensuring leaders are equipped with accurate, timely, and actionable data and insights to support operational and strategic planning and decision-making.

This role translates data, analytics, and industry intelligence into insights that inform pension service delivery, experience design, and operational planning. The role supports organizational planning, prioritization, and performance management by providing scenario modeling, forecasting, and reporting that links outcomes to strategic objectives.

Reporting to the MD, Growth, this role provides the operational planning support and analytical foundation that enables leadership decisions across Growth and Enabling Services, Experience and Specialized Operations. This role also compiles Pension Services data for benchmarking studies and surveys in which UPP participates.

A core focus of the role is strengthening Pension Services’ ability to use data responsibly and effectively, ensuring reporting, forecasting, and analytics capabilities align with UPP’s data governance and AI frameworks while enhancing member and employer value.

This role is based in downtown Toronto under a hybrid work policy, allowing employees the flexibility to work remotely and in-office (min two days per week in-office).

This job posting is for an existing vacancy and is open to Independent Contractors

Note

Target Start Date: First week of January
This role is open to independent contractors paid hourly, if preferred

Specific Accountabilities

The Associate Director, Pension Planning & Performance Reporting will have responsibility for but not limited to the following:

Lead the development and delivery of UPP’s Pension Services reporting and analytics.
Translate data, analytics, and industry intelligence into insights and strategies and lead monthly discussions with the Pension Services leadership team and partners to identify areas of concern, risk and/or opportunity
Provide the analytical foundation for pension service delivery, experience design, and operational planning, equipping leaders with the data required to make evidence-based decisions.
Support the MD, Growth in the analysis, research and execution of the pension operational strategy, delivering insights and reporting (to the Pension Services Committee, Board and Joint Sponsors).
Support organizational planning and prioritization by providing scenario modeling, forecasting, and performance reporting that links outcomes to strategic objectives. Lead monthly and quarterly scorecard reporting development and communication.
Work with UPP Data teams to identify data, reporting, and BI infrastructure requirements and solutions.
Collaborate with Pension Services teams and partners to ensure data and analytics inform growth initiatives and business-as-usual operations.
Ensure Pension Services leverages data and analytics capabilities responsibly and in alignment with UPP’s data governance and AI frameworks.
Drive a culture of continuous improvement and curiosity by empowering teams to use data and analytics to enhance member and employer value.

Qualifications & Experience

Bachelor’s degree required; postgraduate degree is an asset.
Minimum 8-10 years of progressive experience in data analytics, business intelligence, reporting, or pension administration within a regulated environment.
Demonstrated experience developing and communicating performance reporting, forecasting models, and scenario analysis.
Strong understanding of Canadian pension administration and service delivery operations.
Experience working with BI tools and data platforms.
Proficiency in data analysis, reporting, and dashboard development.
Experience supporting executive-level decision-making with structured analytics.
Knowledge of data governance frameworks and regulatory requirements related to pension reporting.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to present complex findings clearly.
Programming or querying experience (e.g., SQL, Python) is an asset.

ATTRIBUTES

Analytical and structured thinker with strong attention to detail and accuracy.
Curious and insight-driven, with a continuous improvement mindset.
Clear communicator capable of translating complex data into practical insights.
Collaborative and cross-functional in approach.
Comfortable operating in ambiguous environments.
Responsible and disciplined in handling sensitive and regulated data.
Focused on enabling informed decision-making and operational transparency.

LIFE AT UPP

Do work that matters.
We are duty-bound to serve our members’ interests, and it’s a responsibility we don’t take lightly. That’s why we’ve ingrained sustainability in our work from day one—to ensure our members have a resilient future to retire into, both today and for generations to come.

Stronger together.
Collaboration is how UPP was born, and it’s how we work with each other and our partners day in, day out. No one at UPP is just a number (even if they are excellent at math) and every win is a shared win.

Grow every day.
You’ll have the opportunity to work on unique, once-in-a-career projects that maximize your skill set and probably teach you some new ones—at any stage in your career.

Benefits

Prioritize wellness.
At UPP, wellness takes many forms. Ultimately, it’s about ensuring our people are cared for in the ways that matter to them. Check out some highlights of our inclusive employee-focused benefits program including:

Defined benefit pension plan
Flexible hybrid work model
Paid time off – vacations, personal days and wellness days
Work remotely up to eight weeks/year
Comprehensive group benefits including medical, dental, vision, etc.
Extended paramedical and mental health service coverage
Health care and lifestyle spending accounts
Fertility treatments, paid parental leave, and gender affirmation coverage
Education Assistance program

This posting will remain open for a minimum of seven (7) days and will remain open until a sufficient number of qualified applications are received or finalist candidates have been identified.

Artificial intelligence (AI) tools may be used to support certain stages of the recruitment process, including sourcing, screening, and assessment. All hiring decisions involve human review and intervention by UPP employees.

UPP enthusiastically welcomes applications from all qualified applicants and especially invites people with lived experience as an Indigenous person, a person with a disability or as a member of another Human Rights Code protected group that faces barriers to employment to apply. Our goal is to create a barrier-free experience for every candidate throughout the recruitment process.

UPP respects your privacy. For information on how UPP handles the personal information you provide during the application process, please see our Job Applicant Privacy Statement.

jobs.title: Vice President Finance
jobs.description:
Position Summary

Our client is a growth-focused organization seeking a Vice President, Finance to join its executive leadership team. The role is based in Oakville, Ontario. This leader owns financial strategy, capital structure, and profitable growth. They act as a trusted partner to the CEO, CFO, Board and investors, and lead FP&A, corporate strategy, corporate development and M&A. They also work with commercial, operations and technology teams to turn financial insight into decisions on pricing, investment and M&A.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Leadership & Executive Partnering

- Partner with the CEO, CFO and executive team to shape multi-year strategy, capital allocation and corporate scorecards.
- Align executive incentives with free cash flow and EBITDA milestones.
- Build quantitative business cases, including payback analyses and market and commercial sizing, for major investments, new service lines and platform or infrastructure modernization.
- Support Board authorization of large investments with clear financial models and go-to-market cases.

Capital Structure, Treasury & M&A

- Lead debt and equity financing, refinancing and capital structure work, including covenant compliance frameworks, liquidity stress-testing and 13-week cash flow forecasting.
- Direct sell-side readiness: normalized Quality of Earnings (QoE) bridges, pro forma EBITDA adjustments, working capital targets and virtual data room preparation.
- Own acquisitions end to end: valuation, financial due diligence, deal close and post-merger integration.
- Build and review valuation and transaction models (three-statement, DCF, LBO, precedent transactions, trading multiples).
- Assess restructuring and recapitalization options, including unit economics, overhead rationalization and debt capacity.

FP&A, Reporting & Analytics

- Run annual budgeting, long-range planning and monthly rolling forecasts.
- Standardize C-suite, Board and sponsor reporting, including Monthly Business Reviews (MBRs), EBITDA bridges and operational KPIs.
- Build executive dashboards for real-time KPI tracking, and set data governance and integrity standards across ERP and CRM systems.
- Lead the financial modeling and rollout of AI and predictive analytics tools, quantifying efficiency gains, productivity lifts and cost takeout.

Commercial Finance & Pricing

- Work with Sales leadership on pricing models, pricing floors and profitability guardrails, and on pipeline and sales reporting.
- Redesign variable commission and incentive compensation plans.
- Formalize contractual price escalation schedules and model multi-year renewals to protect margin.
- Evaluate and structure strategic partnerships and commercial alliances, including ROI modeling and revenue-sharing frameworks.
- Evaluate facility and operational footprint consolidation to reduce recurring overhead.

Accounting & Governance

- Ensure financial reporting complies with US GAAP and IFRS.
- Prepare executive and Audit Committee packages.
- Bring audit-level rigor to financial governance and compliance.

Team Leadership

- Lead, mentor and develop the FP&A team and wider finance staff.
- Provide high-visibility decision support to the CEO, CFO and investors.

Qualifications & Experience

Education & Credentials

- Honours bachelor's degree in science, finance, accounting or a related field.
- CPA, CA designation.
- MBA.

Experience

- Senior finance leadership experience, acting as a close partner to the CEO, CFO and Board.
- Experience in private equity-backed, SaaS/FinTech or tech-enabled services environments, including sponsor reporting and governance.
- Hands-on M&A experience: sell-side readiness, due diligence, valuation and post-merger integration.
- Capital markets and lending experience: leading a major credit facility refinancing, covenant management and liquidity forecasting.
- Commercial finance experience: pricing strategy, incentive compensation design and contract economics.
- Experience quantifying and rolling out AI or predictive analytics initiatives.
- FP&A leadership: has led an FP&A team of 7 and supported CEO, CFO and investor decision-making, and has supervised teams of 3 to 20 staff.
- Background in public accounting, including financial audit under US GAAP and IFRS and transaction due diligence.
- Experience across technology, retail, manufacturing and financial services.
- Scale: has worked on transactions and programs of real size, such as a $300M senior credit facility refinancing, investment cases of $50M+, or due diligence on targets from $20M to $1B+.

Core Competencies

- Strategic financial planning and business case development.
- Private equity governance, Board and business reporting.
- M&A readiness, valuation, diligence and integration.
- Commercial sales finance, pricing and compensation structuring.
- AI and predictive analytics rollout, with data governance across ERP and CRM systems.
- Clear communication of complex financial narratives to the Board, executives and non-financial stakeholders.

jobs.title: Director, Enterprise Solutions - Google Cloud
jobs.description:
About Apply

APPLY is the Agentic Customer Experience (ACx) partner for the world's most ambitious consumer and entertainment brands. We bring together deep domain expertise across Retail, CPG, Sports, and Media with AI-native delivery capability, designing and delivering agentic solutions that turn CX vision into commercial reality. We are the partner of choice for brands like Arc'teryx, NFL, Lululemon, and Kraft Heinz. For more information, visit applydigital.com .

LOCATION:
APPLY is hybrid/remote friendly. The preferred candidate should be based in Canada, working in hours that align to ET (Eastern Timezone)
.

THE ROLE:

As Director, Enterprise Solutions - Google Cloud, you'll drive how Apply Digital shapes, sells, and delivers complex cloud and AI solutions on Google Cloud for enterprise clients. Reporting into the VP, Enterprise Solutions, you'll bridge technical architecture, business strategy, and go-to-market execution. You'll be a hands-on architect and trusted technology advisor to client executives while driving co-sell engagement with Google Cloud's partner engineering, product, and field sales teams. You'll also help build and grow Apply Digital's internal Google Cloud community of practitioners, helping enterprise organizations use Gemini, Vertex AI, BigQuery, and cloud-native platforms to create meaningful business value and competitive advantage.

Responsibilities

Strategic Leadership & Solution Architecture

Shape and execute the technology vision for enterprise clients on Google Cloud, aligning AI, data, and modernization solutions with business objectives and transformation goals
Lead and personally contribute to the design and architecture of complex, enterprise-level solutions using Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, Vertex AI, BigQuery, AlloyDB, GKE, and Cloud Run
Provide technical leadership and guidance on architecture best practices, emerging technologies, and industry trends
Design next-generation agentic and generative AI solutions, including RAG pipelines, multi-agent workflows, and Gemini Enterprise implementations
Define architecture strategies that ensure scalability, security, resilience, and long-term value, including composable and API-first approaches where they fit

Client Relationship Management

Act as a trusted technology advisor to client executives and senior stakeholders
Build CFO-ready TCO and ROI models comparing on-premise, multi-cloud, and Google Cloud unit economics
Lead discovery sessions, architecture reviews, solution design workshops, and technical presentations to align stakeholders on solution vision and approach
Proactively identify opportunities to deliver additional value and expand Apply Digital's footprint within accounts

Pre-Sales Leadership & Revenue Growth

Own pre-sales execution for assigned enterprise pursuits, including discovery, solution design, and proof-of-concept (PoC) engagements
Partner with Apply Digital sellers and Google Cloud account teams to co-sell solutions, carrying a personal pipeline generation and revenue influence goal
Produce RFP responses, Statements of Work, and technical proposals with explicit assumptions, bounded scope, and risk frameworks that protect delivery margins
Use modern AI tools to speed up documentation, proposal drafting, and estimation without sacrificing engineering rigor

Google Cloud Ecosystem & GTM Alignment

Build and maintain strong relationships with Google Cloud Partner Engineers, Product Managers, and Field Sales to maximize joint deal routing and co-sell priority
Contribute to and participate in Quarterly Business Reviews and joint account planning to align Apply Digital's offerings with Google Cloud's strategic priorities, such as Data, Generative AI, and Modernization
Represent Apply Digital at Google Cloud Next, industry events, webinars, and partner panels

Solution Productization & Practice IP

Identify high-value patterns across engagements and help package them into repeatable offerings, accelerators, reference architectures, and pricing models
Develop reusable estimation models, discovery frameworks, and PoC templates that raise the technical output of the broader team
Help build and grow Apply Digital's internal Google Cloud community of practice

Technical Delivery & Project Oversight

Provide delivery leadership for the Google Cloud engagements you shape, ensuring they meet client requirements, quality standards, and business outcomes
Guide technical teams through complex implementation challenges and ensure adherence to Google Cloud best practices

Team Leadership & Development

Mentor and coach junior and mid-level architects on technical design, ecosystem navigation, and commercial pre-sales discipline
Support Google Cloud certification and delivery enablement across the technology team
Contribute to hiring, onboarding, and retention of top Google Cloud talent

Requirements

10+ years of experience in cloud architecture, enterprise solution architecture, or technical consulting in a professional services environment, with at least 2 years in a leadership role
3+ years of dedicated experience in the Google Cloud ecosystem in a customer- and partner-facing capacity
Google Cloud Professional Cloud Architect certification
Proven pre-sales track record, including shaping complex technical deals, writing SOWs, and partnering with sales teams to hit revenue targets
Proven track record of successfully delivering complex solutions for large-scale enterprise clients
Experience working in digital agencies, strategic consultancies, or systems integrators delivering client-facing solutions
Deep, hands-on expertise in modern cloud architectures, database systems (BigQuery, AlloyDB, Cloud Spanner), and containerization platforms (GKE, Cloud Run)
Hands-on production experience with modern AI stacks, such as Vertex AI, Gemini Enterprise, agentic workflows, or RAG pipelines
Ability to build CFO-ready TCO and ROI models
Excellent communication skills with the ability to engage executives, technical stakeholders, and Google Cloud partner teams
Experience mentoring and developing technical team members
Demonstrated ability to manage multiple high-stakes pursuits and client relationships at once
Entrepreneurial mindset with comfort navigating ambiguity and solving complex problems

Nice to Have

Additional Google Cloud certifications (Professional Data Engineer, Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer, or Professional Machine Learning Engineer)
Deep understanding of Gemini Enterprise, Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, Gemini Enterprise for Customer Experience, and Google's generative media offerings
Vertical experience in CPG, Retail, Media, or Entertainment
Experience with commerce platforms, content management systems, and digital experience platforms
Knowledge of agile methodologies and experience leading agile delivery teams
Public speaking experience and thought leadership contributions to the technology or Google Cloud community

$150,000 - $220,000 a year

LIFE AT APPLY

People are at the core of everything we do at APPLY. We provide you with modern tools, systems and approaches, value your time, safety, and health, and strive to build a work community where you can thrive and grow. Here are a few benefits we offer to support you:

Agentic Delivery:
Our people work in a modern way to deliver client outcomes. Broaden your skills on a range of engagements with international brands that have a global impact.

An inclusive and safe environment:
We’re truly committed to building a culture where you are celebrated and everyone feels welcome and safe.

AI & Strategic Upskilling:
Accelerate your professional growth with generous training budgets and mentorship, with a specific focus on Agentic AI expertise and the critical human skills required for the future of work.

Generous vacation policy:
Work-life balance is key to our team’s success, so we offer flexible personal time off (PTO); allowing ample time away from work to promote overall well-being.

Customizable benefits:
Tailor your extended health and dental plan to your needs, priorities, and preferences.

Flexible work arrangements:
We work in a variety of ways, from remote, to in-office, to a blend of both.

APPLY is a safe, respectful, and inclusive community where differences are celebrated. We are committed to equal opportunity and fostering a workplace where everyone belongs. jobs.description:
Job Description

What is the opportunity?

Join our U.S. Technology Strategy and Architecture team as Director, Technology Product Strategy, where you will play a key role in supporting the development and execution of technology strategy across RBC’s U.S. organization.

Working closely with U.S. Technology Strategy & Architecture leadership, business lines, technology teams, and enterprise architecture, you will help shape the strategic direction of the U.S. technology organization. You will analyze the technology landscape, support strategic planning and investment decisions, and work across business and technology teams to advance key priorities.

This role provides broad exposure across the U.S. technology organization and an opportunity to work on some of its most important strategic questions. You will combine structured problem solving, technology knowledge, stakeholder management, and executive communication to support senior leaders in making informed technology decisions and advancing the U.S. technology agenda.

What will you do?

Support target-state strategy development: Partner with Technology Strategy & Architecture leadership to develop and maintain forward-looking U.S. technology strategy and, where required, business-line technology strategies. Gather inputs, assess strategic alternatives, and translate direction into clear target-state objectives, principles, KPIs, and priorities.
Maintain a view of the technology estate: Develop and maintain a comprehensive view of the U.S. technology landscape, bringing together information on applications, platforms, infrastructure, capabilities, dependencies, and investments to support strategic planning and decision-making.
Conduct strategic analyses: Perform structured, point-in-time analyses of technology opportunities, challenges, and strategic questions. Synthesize quantitative and qualitative information, evaluate alternatives, and develop recommendations for leadership consideration.
Support strategic alignment: Work with business and technology stakeholders to assess the alignment of major initiatives, programs, and investments with U.S. technology strategy and enterprise priorities. Identify potential gaps or areas of misalignment and support development of appropriate actions.
Support roadmap and funding decisions: Develop analyses and decision materials that help leadership evaluate technology roadmaps, investment priorities, dependencies, trade-offs, and funding requirements.
Support architecture governance and control: Partner with Enterprise Architecture and technology teams to facilitate architecture governance activities, track strategic and architectural decisions, identify areas requiring escalation, and support alignment with established architecture principles and target states.
Coordinate strategic planning activities: Support recurring strategy, roadmap, portfolio, and governance processes across the U.S. technology organization, ensuring stakeholders have the information and analysis required to make timely decisions.
Develop executive-level materials: Translate complex technology topics into concise presentations, recommendations, business cases, and decision materials for senior technology and business leadership.
Monitor strategic progress: Develop and maintain KPIs, KRIs, and other measures that provide visibility into progress against technology strategies, roadmaps, strategic initiatives, and architectural objectives.
Build organizational capability: Support the development and adoption of frameworks, methodologies, tools, templates, and ways of working that strengthen technology strategy and architecture capabilities across the U.S. organization.
Facilitate cross-functional collaboration: Coordinate across business lines, technology teams, architecture, finance, risk, and other stakeholders to gather inputs, resolve issues, and support decisions on cross-cutting technology priorities.
Identify emerging issues and opportunities: Analyze trends across the technology estate and external technology landscape to identify potential capability gaps, duplication, architectural constraints, emerging technologies, and opportunities for strategic improvement.

What do you need to succeed?

Must have:

Undergraduate degree or equivalent experience in technology, business, engineering, finance, or a related field.
10+ years of experience across technology strategy, enterprise architecture, technology transformation, management consulting, technology program management, or related disciplines.
Strong strategic and analytical capabilities, with demonstrated experience structuring ambiguous problems and developing fact-based recommendations.
Ability to understand complex technology environments and connect technology considerations to broader business and strategic objectives.
Experience supporting technology strategies, roadmaps, business cases, investment decisions, operating models, or transformation initiatives.
Strong executive communication skills, including the ability to synthesize complex information into clear presentations and decision materials.
Strong stakeholder management skills and demonstrated ability to work effectively across business and technology organizations.
Ability to manage multiple priorities and deliver high-quality work in a complex, matrixed environment.
Strong understanding of technology and/or the financial services industry.
Experience using current AI tooling to support research, automate repetitive tasks, analyze large data sets, etc.

Nice to have:

Experience in financial services or another highly regulated industry.
Experience in a matrix environment, such as a large, publicly traded corporation.

What’s in it for you?

We thrive on the challenge to be our best, progressive thinking to keep growing, and working together to deliver trusted advice to help our clients thrive and communities prosper. We care about each other, reaching our potential, making a difference to our communities, and achieving success that is mutual.

A comprehensive Total Rewards Program including bonuses and flexible benefits, competitive compensation, commissions, and stock where applicable.
Leaders who support your development through coaching and managing opportunities.
Ability to make a difference and lasting impact.
Work in a dynamic, collaborative, progressive, and high-performing team.
A world-class training program in financial services.

jobs.description:
Company Description

VOSKER is a North American leader in remote area surveillance.

Every day, we’re proud to help our customers keep an eye on what truly matters to them by developing solar-powered, cellular-connected cameras integrated with our exclusive platform.

In a few words, at VOSKER: we perform, we think differently, and we take care of our people. We leverage our expertise to win as a team and redefine what’s possible!

What We Offer

A work environment where your ideas come to life and your ambitions take flight
A dynamic, non-routine daily life every day is different, and that’s what makes it exciting!
A hybrid work model: work from home or from one of our offices it’s your choice
The opportunity to work remotely from abroad for up to 3 months (90 days)
Access to a learning platform to grow your skills on company time
A wellness account to reimburse expenses related to your health, passions, and interests
Free 24/7 access to online healthcare professionals and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
Comprehensive group insurance including vision and dental, 50% paid by the employer
A group RRSP with employer contributions
Parental leave top-up for new parents
Vacation based on your total years of professional experience

Job Description

Fair compensation, benefits that make a difference in our people’s lives, and data that informs decisions: at VOSKER, you’ll have the chance to shape all of this.

As the head of total compensation and reporting to the Head of Culture and Organizational Performance, you’ll be a trusted partner in a role that’s both strategic and highly hands-on. If you enjoy influencing decisions without losing sight of the big picture, this position is for you.

What’s In Store For You:

Compensation: Define and implement VOSKER’s compensation policies in the context of growth and the integration of current (Estonia or Germany) or future acquisitions.
Business Partnership: Support the teams’ needs regarding salary recommendations, salary benchmarking, annual raises, bonus plans and long-term incentive programs, pay equity, and business intelligence.
Employee Benefits and Savings: Develop our programs, negotiate contracts, and manage external partners (Dialogue, Industrielle Alliance, Solertia, etc.) .
Data and HRIS: Analyze and share key metrics with the Talent & Culture team and senior management. Support the systems administration team in governing T&C data via the HRIS (UKG Pro) and oversee the deployment of new HRIS modules as needed.
Mergers and Acquisitions: Participate in due diligence and the integration of upcoming projects.
Budget: Participate in establishing annual payroll and benefits budgets with the Finance team.
Promoting the Value Proposition: Collaborate with colleagues in the Culture Promotion team to foster transparency and highlight the value proposition to employees.
Leadership and Strategic Oversight: Motivate and guide the total compensation team and its members, while staying abreast of emerging market trends and compensation governance practices.

Qualifications

Key Qualifications

You hold a bachelor’s degree in human resources management, finance, actuarial science, or any other relevant field.
You have held a strategic position in compensation management for at least 7 years, with solid knowledge of employee benefits, long-term incentive plans, and retirement savings.
You are comfortable taking on a cross-functional role that involves frequent and complex collaboration with various departments.
You have a strong ability to influence both senior management and the entire workforce, and you can communicate the company’s compensation vision in both French and English (written and oral).
You want to play a strategic role while remaining firmly grounded in hands-on work and execution.

Plus Points

You have experience in an international environment and in integrating new entities following acquisitions (strongly preferred).
You are committed to delivering a distinctive employee experience and find creative solutions to the situations that arise.
You have a good sense of humor and the desire to take on this very serious role without taking yourself too seriously!

WHAT WE OFFER

A high-impact role in a fast-growing company, at the heart of integrating new teams across Europe.
An international setting and a variety of challenges: compensation, benefits, data, and onboarding.
A culture where we take our work seriously, but not ourselves.
A hybrid work model that involves working in downtown Montreal at least once a week, occasionally in Victoriaville, and from home on other days.

Additional Information

EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER

At VOSKER, we value the uniqueness of every individual and celebrate the diversity that helps us redefine what’s possible. We foster collaboration in a healthy, inclusive work environment where all voices are heard.

jobs.title: Director of Portfolio Finance
jobs.description:
The opportunity

We are building a centralized finance function for our portfolio, and we are looking for the person to lead it. You will give Rhyno greater control over cash, faster and more reliable reporting, and the financial credibility to work with lenders and financing partners from a position of strength.
This role suits someone who is comfortable deep in the numbers and equally comfortable stepping back to tell the partners clearly what they see: where each business stands, what healthy looks like, and how far there is to go.

What you will do

1. Treasury and liquidity

Own rolling 13-week cash flow forecasts across all six companies, refreshed weekly with variance analysis against actuals.
Build the 12 to 24 month liquidity outlook that feeds budgets and planning.
Manage AP prioritization and supplier payment plans and monitor bank accounts and cash daily.
Track available credit and covenant headroom under base and downside cases and flag liquidity risks early.
Manage banking relationships, account structures and intercompany funding across the portfolio.

2. Financial reporting
Accelerate month-end and annual financial reporting across the portfolio.
Improve consolidation, and set a common reporting template, chart of accounts mapping and reporting calendar for every company.
Produce a weekly liquidity view and a monthly reporting package for Rhyno leadership.
Set the cadence and content of financial reporting for board meetings.
Coordinate year-end audits with external auditors.

3. Budgeting and forecasting
Lead the annual budget for each company and for the consolidated portfolio.
Run rolling forecasts and monthly variance analysis and hold company leaders accountable to plan.
Benchmark each company's P&L against a healthy business in its space and set clear targets for where it should be.

4. Operational advisory
Identify cash flow inefficiencies across receivables, payables and inventory, and set working capital targets with each company.
Tie project billing (schedules of billings, progress draws and holdbacks) to cash so invoicing moves on time.
Advise leadership on operational resizing and cost reductions.
Find quick wins across the portfolio in financial systems, operations and management practices.
Strengthen financial controls, including payment approvals, signing authority and fraud prevention.

jobs.title: Global Head of Cloud Platform Engineering
jobs.description:
About Innocap

Innocap is the leading Dedicated Managed Account Platform (DMAP) globally, providing institutional allocators with a superior way to structure, access, and oversee their alternative investments. With over US$135 billion on the platform and more than 570 employees across the globe, we are transforming how allocators access and manage alternative investments.

Powered by our people, processes and purpose‑built technology, Innocap is seeking forward-thinking individuals to join us on our exciting journey. At Innocap, you won't just manage what’s here today. You’ll build what comes next. Here, careers are about building, not maintaining.

We give our people the freedom to think boldly, move quickly, and create real impact with less red tape. Driven by transformation, trust and collaboration, we never settle for the status quo and are constantly finding better ways to serve our clients and actively shape the future of the investment industry.

At Innocap, your work makes a difference every day – and helps build what’s next for our clients, the industry, and your career.

Because the future doesn’t build itself. We do.

About The Role

As Global Head of Cloud Platform Engineering, reporting to the Chief Technology Officer, you will own Innocap’s cloud runtime, developer platform, SRE practices, observability, cloud security guardrails, technology recovery and cloud economics. You will build and lead a high-leverage global engineering function that operates a secure, resilient and economical cloud estate and provides shared capabilities that make engineering teams faster and more effective.

Your mandate will be to provide global leadership, ownership and accountability across the following areas:

Cloud Infrastructure, Runtime and Scaling

The architecture, provisioning, secure connectivity and operational health of Innocap’s cloud infrastructure, primarily Microsoft Azure, including container and compute platforms, managed services, storage, networking and hybrid connectivity.
Capacity forecasting, cloud quotas, workload isolation and headroom, together with secure and scalable runtime foundations and compute orchestration for data and AI platforms, including appropriate identity, access, consumption, telemetry and emergency controls.

Developer Platform and Engineering Enablement

Declarative infrastructure provisioning, reusable CI/CD pipelines, artifact management, environment promotion, deployment validation and rollback, with configuration drift eliminated and exceptions visible and time bound.
Shared source-control and build-platform foundations, repository guardrails, build-agent security, artifact integrity, dependency and secret-scanning integrations, and the lifecycle of non-production and test environments.
Provide documented, reusable and self-service workflows for provisioning, deployment, access, test data and troubleshooting, and measure paved-road adoption, developer satisfaction, provisioning lead time and time saved.

Reliability, Observability, and Technology Recovery

The unified observability stack, telemetry standards and end-to-end service-level visibility; establish and govern SLOs, SLIs and error budgets; and lead major technology incident coordination, blameless postmortems and root-cause closure.
Establish production-readiness standards, named service ownership, sustainable on-call coverage and escalation; maintain an authoritative service inventory, architecture documentation and executable operational runbooks; and reduce alert noise, repeat incidents and operational toil.
Infrastructure backups, immutable recovery capabilities and failover mechanisms aligned with business-agreed RTOs and RPOs; run evidenced restore tests and coordinated technical recovery exercises and validate application and data recovery with domain teams.

Reliability Cloud Security and Audit Readiness

Engineer and operate cloud security guardrails, policy as code, scanning, detection integrations, environment isolation, IAM and RBAC, privileged access, secrets, encryption and key-lifecycle controls in partnership with Cybersecurity.
Automated patching, supported-version maintenance and vulnerability-remediation SLAs across shared platform components; automate continuous control-evidence collection for SOC 2 requirements and institutional client due diligence.

Cloud Economics and Technical Vendors

Cloud FinOps, including cost visibility and allocation, forecasting, budget alerting, commitment discounts, right-sizing, waste elimination and meaningful workload unit costs; serve as technical and operational owner for core cloud, data-platform runtime, observability and managed-service vendors.

Cloud Platform Strategy and Organizational Leadership

Define and execute a rolling platform roadmap aligned with business growth, application modernization and operational risk, including shared platform architecture, investment priorities, technical-debt reduction, supported patterns, versioning, upgrade paths, deprecation and retirement of unsupported infrastructure.
Build and develop a high-performing global engineering team with clear ownership, strong technical leadership, succession and sustainable support coverage; reduce key-person dependency and balance internal capability with managed services and specialist partners.
The function’s operating plan, staffing strategy and budget; make capacity allocation between operations, reliability improvement and roadmap delivery explicit; prevent urgent support from permanently displacing platform development; and report outcomes through a scorecard covering reliability, recovery, delivery stability, developer adoption, operational toil and unit cost.

Primary Qualifications & Skills

10+ years of experience in cloud infrastructure, platform engineering, DevOps or SRE, including 5+ years leading global platform or infrastructure teams in data-intensive, high-availability environments. Financial services, fintech, capital markets or institutional data-platform experience is strongly preferred.
Deep architectural expertise in Microsoft Azure, including AKS, networking, Entra ID/IAM, Key Vault and managed services, with modern infrastructure-as-code and CI/CD practices using tools such as Terraform or Bicep and GitHub or Azure DevOps.
Demonstrated success building reusable self-service platforms, improving developer productivity, establishing production-readiness and on-call practices, and delivering measurable reliability and recovery improvements.
Experience operating distributed data or compute platforms and enterprise observability tooling with disciplined cost and performance governance. Databricks and Datadog experience is an asset; equivalent platform experience is relevant.
Experience with SOC 2 control requirements or comparable assurance frameworks, institutional-grade disaster recovery, change control and auditability.
Proven ability to develop teams, prioritize a roadmap, manage budgets and vendors, translate cloud consumption into unit economics, and make pragmatic build-versus-buy and simplicity-versus-complexity decisions.
A technically credible player-coach who eliminates manual toil, measures outcomes, develops others and enables application teams rather than creating a centralized approval or ticket-taking bottleneck.
Excellent communication and stakeholder-management skills, with the ability to influence engineering leaders and translate technical priorities, risks and economics for business leaders.

Innocap is an equal opportunity employer. We are dedicated to hiring diverse talent and fostering an inclusive, equitable, and people-first culture where everyone feels valued, respected, and empowered to contribute fully – regardless of their background. With employees across the globe, we firmly believe that the unique perspectives and strengths of our people help us grow stronger and allow us to better serve our clients.

If you require accommodation at any stage during your application process, please let us know.

jobs.title: Assistant Vice President / Vice President, Project Finance & Infrastructure
jobs.description:
The Role

Morningstar DBRS is seeking an experienced credit professional to join its Project Finance & Infrastructure team at the Assistant Vice President or Vice President level in Toronto. This role offers an opportunity to lead and support rating assignments across a diversified portfolio of North American infrastructure assets, including conventional power and renewable energy, digital infrastructure, transportation, public-private partnerships (PPPs), and other project finance and infrastructure sectors.

Reporting to the Managing Director - Asset, Project, & Sports Finance (Toronto), you will analyze and monitor a portfolio of project finance and infrastructure ratings.. You will evaluate transaction structures, financial performance, contractual arrangements, and credit risks while developing well-supported recommendations for rating committees.

Working closely with colleagues in Toronto, New York, and across the global organization, you will work in an environment that values rigorous analytical thinking, open dialogue and professional growth, while gaining significant exposure to issuers, sponsors, investors, and advisors and other stakeholders across the North American infrastructure landscape.

We are considering candidates at both the Assistant Vice President and Vice President levels, with final leveling determined by experience, credit expertise, and demonstrated ability to independently lead rating assignments and manage complex transactions.

What You'll Be Doing

Analyze and monitor a diversified portfolio of project finance and infrastructure ratings, including new transactions and ongoing surveillance, with a particular focus on Canadian infrastructure assets.
Serve as a lead or supporting rating analyst across conventional power and renewable energy, digital infrastructure, transportation, PPPs, and other infrastructure sectors.
Review and interpret transaction documentation, including power purchase agreements, concession agreements, financing agreements, legal opinions, and other contractual arrangements, to assess credit implications.
Perform comprehensive financial statement analysis and evaluate project finance models, including cash flow forecasts, sensitivity analyses, and downside scenarios.
Prepare high-quality credit rating reports, press releases, research notes, and analytical commentary that clearly communicate key credit drivers and risks.
Develop rating committee materials, formulate credit recommendations, and present analytical findings and recommendations to rating committees.
Engage with issuers, sponsors, investors, and advisors to discuss credit performance, rating rationales, and analytical methodologies.
Manage ongoing portfolio surveillance, monitoring financial performance, industry developments, and emerging credit risks.
Contribute to the development, refinement, and application of project finance rating methodologies and sector-specific analytical approaches.
Support analytical discussions with fixed-income investors and provide analytical support for business development initiatives.
Work collaboratively with colleagues across Europe and North America across the broader Fundamental Ratings team, in particular the Diversified Industries and Energy & Natural Resources groups.
Collaborate with colleagues across the global Project Finance & Infrastructure team and contribute to knowledge-sharing and the development of junior analysts.

What We're Looking For

Bachelor's degree in finance, business, economics, engineering, or a related discipline.
At least five years of relevant financial or credit analysis experience, including a minimum of two years of experience in project finance, infrastructure finance, or corporate credit analysis.
Strong understanding of credit risk assessment, financial markets, and project finance or corporate financing structures.
Relevant credit experience gained at a credit rating agency, bank, infrastructure advisory or consulting firm, or investment management firm. Prior rating agency experience while not required, is an asset
Experience across one or more infrastructure sectors, including conventional power and renewable energy, digital infrastructure, transportation, or PPPs, is preferred.
Strong financial modeling and financial statement analysis skills, including the ability to evaluate cash flow projections, debt structures, and sensitivity scenarios.
Experience reviewing financing agreements, legal contracts, and other transaction documentation from a credit perspective.
Strong research, analytical, and problem-solving capabilities with exceptional attention to detail.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to present complex credit analysis and recommendations to senior stakeholders.
Strong analytical judgment and the ability to develop, articulate, and defend well-supported credit recommendations.
Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced, team-oriented environment.
Familiarity with North American infrastructure financing markets, particularly Canadian infrastructure and PPP transactions, is an asset.
Completion of, or progress toward, the CFA designation or an MBA is an asset.
Willingness to travel as required.

Base Salary Compensation Range - AVP

$82,000.00-120,000.00

Incentive Target Percentage

20% Annual

Base Salary Compensation Range - VP

$109,489.00-160,711.00

Incentive Target Percentage

30% Annual

For consideration at the Vice President level, candidates should have 7+ years of relevant experience in project finance and infrastructure finance credit analysis, demonstrate strong analytical judgment and the ability to independently lead complex credit assessments, manage rating assignments, and present credit recommendations to rating committees. Experience providing analytical guidance to junior team members is also preferred.

The Group

Our Project Finance & Infrastructure team provides independent credit ratings and research across a broad range of infrastructure assets throughout North America. The team's coverage includes conventional power and renewable energy projects, digital infrastructure such as data centers, telecommunications towers and fiber networks, transportation assets including airports, toll roads and ports, and public-private partnerships.

Through fundamental credit analysis, financial modeling, transaction structuring expertise, and ongoing surveillance, the team evaluates the creditworthiness of infrastructure projects and provides independent credit opinions that support informed decisions by issuers, investors, lenders, and other market participants.

About Us

Morningstar DBRS is a leading provider of independent rating services and opinions for corporate and sovereign entities, financial institutions, and project and structured finance instruments globally. Rating more than 4,000 issuers and 60,000 securities, it is one of the top four credit rating agencies in the world.

Morningstar DBRS empowers investor success by bringing more transparency and a much-needed diversity of opinion in the credit rating industry. Our approach and size allow us to be nimble enough to respond to customers' needs in their local markets, but large enough to provide the necessary expertise and resources they require. Market innovators choose to work with us because of our agility, tech-forward approach, and exceptional customer service.

Morningstar DBRS is the next generation of credit ratings.

If you receive and accept an offer from us, we require that personal and any related investments be disclosed confidentiality to our Compliance team (days vary by region). These investments will be reviewed to ensure they meet Code of Ethics requirements. If any conflicts of interest are identified, then you will be required to liquidate those holdings immediately. In addition, dependent on your department and location of work certain employee accounts must be held with an approved broker (for example all, U.S. employee accounts). If this applies and your account(s) are not with an approved broker, you will be required to move your holdings to an approved broker.

Morningstar's hybrid work environment gives you the opportunity to collaborate in-person each week as we've found that we're at our best when we're purposely together on a regular basis. In most of our locations, our hybrid work model is four days in-office each week. A range of other benefits are also available to enhance flexibility as needs change. No matter where you are, you'll have tools and resources to engage meaningfully with your global colleagues.

What’s the Opportunity?

Newcomers are critical client segment for RBC, with distinct needs across their journey - from preparing to move to Canada, to establishing their financial lives upon arrival, to building deeper financial relationships as they settle and grow.

As Director, Newcomer Channel Strategy & Operations
, you will lead the strategy and evolution of the channels, capabilities and partnership operations required to deliver a differentiated newcomer banking proposition. You will own the "how" behind our newcomer strategy: translating our ambition into intuitive client journeys, scalable capabilities, effective frontline experiences and an ecosystem of services that helps newcomers establish their lives in Canada.

This is a highly cross-functional role. You will work across Everyday Banking & Client Growth, Product, Digital, Enablement, Advice Centre, Technology, Risk, Compliance, Marketing, and external partners to identify friction, establish priorities, and mobilize the organization around a multi-year newcomer journey.

What You'll Do

Own the End-To-End Newcomer Onboarding Experience

Develop and continuously evolve the target experience for newcomers across key moments in their journey - from pre-arrival through onboarding, settlement, and early relationship growth
Map and assess end-to-end newcomer journeys across digital, assisted, and non-traditional channels
Identify the highest impact experience gaps, friction points, and capability opportunities
Define the target state newcomer experience and work cross-functionally to define it into a prioritized roadmap

Clarify documentation, identification, residency and eligibility requirements
Challenge legacy processes and distinguish true regulatory requirements from internal practices

Work with distribution leaders to understand frontline friction and execution gaps

Simplify complex policies and product information

The Finance Director serves as a strategic business partner to the Leadership Team in support of Husky’s Global Service Business and Customer Success Management strategy. This role provides leadership for financial planning, forecasting, performance analysis, governance, and decision support to drive profitable growth, improve operational performance, and strengthen financial visibility across service revenue streams, including field service, contracts, parts, and other aftermarket offerings. Performance Management & Analysis

Ensure alignment with corporate finance requirements, accounting policies, and internal controls

Experience in a service, aftermarket, field service, maintenance, or contract-based business strongly preferred.
Strong financial modeling, forecasting, and business analysis skills.

Executive presence with strong communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills, and the ability to influence senior leaders across functions and regions.

Transformation Governance & Strategic Execution

Partner with senior leaders to translate approved priorities into executable workstream plans.
Establish and maintain governance processes supporting prioritization, intake, qualification, approval, and execution oversight.
Drive accountability and follow-through on decisions arising from governance forums.
Coordinate cross-functional stakeholders to ensure alignment of delivery plans, dependencies, milestones, and outcomes.

Evaluate transformation opportunities against strategic objectives, capacity constraints, risk considerations, and value criteria.
Facilitate portfolio planning processes and support leadership decision-making.
Maintain visibility into transformation demand, delivery capacity, investment priorities, and execution status.

Adoption & Value Realization

Define and implement measurement frameworks for technology, automation, AI, and Data transformation initiatives.
Establish and report on key performance indicators measuring adoption, utilization, business outcomes, benefits realization, and operational effectiveness.
Develop methodologies for measuring product value, customer value, business impact, and sustained adoption.
Monitor trends and identify opportunities to improve user adoption and business outcomes.
Partner with product owners, business stakeholders, and transformation leaders to address adoption barriers and optimize value realization.

Operating Model & Process Excellence

Design and formalize governance operating models supporting transformation management and execution oversight.
Develop and maintain RASCIs, Standard Operating Procedures, playbooks, operating frameworks, qualification frameworks, intake processes, and governance documentation.
Establish repeatable and scalable operating practices across transformation portfolios.
Drive continuous improvement initiatives that improve governance effectiveness and execution efficiency.

Reporting, Insights & Performance Management

Establish and execute recurring reporting cycles covering adoption performance, benefits realization, capacity utilization, portfolio performance, transformation progress, and product value realization.
Develop dashboards, scorecards, and management reporting for executive audiences.
